prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Please help! Monstera Prop not going well?

Tl;Dr I tried to save my dying monstera by propagating the only healthy looking bits that were left. It's been in a jug of water with spagham moss, water gets changed regularly, it's been 3 weeks and I have no roots yet..

After a week or two of it not recovering, I decided I needed to do emergency surgery. I watched some YouTube videos on propagating monstera and I cut the "middle" section out of the plant, as that's where the "healthiest" looking leaves remained. I used a clean, fresh razor blade to make the cuts and did exactly as the video said... I have changed the water out every 3-4 days. The leaves still look unchanged, no better or worse, but there are no signs of new roots or new growth anywhere and the areas that were cut have just turned brown...

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
Your cutting isn't necessarily doomed, but a few things are working against it. Here's what I see in the photos.

## What's going wrong

**1. The cutting has no nodes at the base.**
Monstera roots and grows only from a **node**, the bump on the stem where a leaf and aerial root attach. In your close-ups the bottom of the cutting is a long, bare section of petiole (leaf stalk) and stem with a dark, mushy cut face. Without a node at or below the waterline, a cutting can sit green for months and never root. This is probably the main problem. A leaf and petiole alone will never make a new plant.

**2. The cut ends are rotting.**
The dark, glossy, slimy brown patches on the cut face and along the stem are rot, not normal callusing. A healthy cut dries and calluses, or stays pale and firm. This probably comes from the cutting sitting in water for 3 weeks, plus whatever caused the original decline, since the mother plant was already stressed or sick.

**3. The mother plant was already dying.**
If the original problem was root rot (common with big monsteras in pots with a saucer or in soggy soil), the stem tissue may be infected too. That would explain why the "healthy-looking" section isn't responding.

## What I'd do

1. **Check the nodes.** Look at the stem for brown bumps, often with an aerial root nub, opposite where each leaf attaches. If your cutting has one, trim just below it.
2. **Cut back to clean tissue.** Remove the rotted section until the inside is firm and pale green or white, with no brown or mush. Use clean, sterilized blades.
3. **Let it callus for a few hours** before putting it back in water.
4. **Keep only the node in water**, not the whole stem. Use a clear jar, and a pinch of cinnamon or a drop of diluted hydrogen peroxide can help limit bacteria.
5. **Give it warmth and bright indirect light.** Roots come slowly in cool or dim conditions.
6. **Don't give up on the mother plant.** Your last photo shows a large plant in a pot with a drainage hole. Unpot it, check the roots, trim any black or mushy ones, and repot in fresh, chunky, well-draining mix. Root rot is a common reason monsteras decline, and any remaining stem with nodes can be cut and rooted too.

## Realistic outlook

If this cutting truly has no node, it won't root, and the leaf will slowly yellow and die. If you find a node on the lower stem, you have a good chance. Also look at the rest of the mother plant: any stem section with a node, even without a leaf, can root and grow.

If you post a photo of the mother plant's roots and the stem with the nodes marked, people can give more specific advice.
